money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Mauritanian Ouguiya (MRU). It's illegal to import or export ouguiyas. You must declare any foreign currency on arrival, but there are no limits on how much you can import. When you leave Mauritania, you can't have more foreign currency with you than the amount you declared on arrival. Credit cards aren't widely used. Traveller's cheques aren't accepted. Most places only accept cash. Some banks in Nouakchott have ATMs which accept foreign credit cards. Check ATM locations with your bank before you travel. items.text: Although Mauritania operates a de facto moratorium on the use of the death penalty, under its penal code, the death penalty can apply for treason, murder, blasphemous speech, sacrilegious acts, and same-sex relationships between men, which are all illegal.
Public displays of affection can cause offence, particularly: in rural and traditional areas near mosques, shrines and religious educational institutions

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Islam is the state religion: unauthorised non-Islamic gatherings and proselytising are illegal, and blasphemy carries a maximum penalty of death. Alcohol and pork are banned for everyone; bags are scanned on arrival. During Ramadan do not eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in public in daytime. Dress modestly off the beach (women cover shoulders, no short skirts; men no sleeveless tops or shorts). Ask before photographing people; never photograph security sites. Same-sex activity between men can carry the death penalty. Carry ID copies, especially outside Nouakchott.
